글:
T3.6 What to do with this on Monday

[표 13. 이 장의 개념이 실제로 쓰이는 자리]
개념 | 쓰이는 블록 | 무엇을 정하나
MTBF · 결정시간상수 | Every asynchronous boundary | Synchroniser depth, and the number you write in the datasheet
동기화기깊이 | Architecture, per crossing | Two by default; three above ~1 GHz or when τ is poorly characterised
다중비트문제 · 그레이코드 | FIFO pointers, counters, status words | Whether the crossing needs an encoding, a handshake, or a FIFO
핸드셰이크 · 비동기FIFO | Streaming data between domains | Latency and depth, and therefore area
리셋동기화기 · 리커버리 | Every clock domain | Whether the block starts in a legal state at every corner
CDC검증 · 준정적신호 | Signoff and the deliverable | The waiver list the integrator inherits

Two numbers end this chapter, and they are the ones to carry: at 1 GHz a
 single-stage crossing fails about once every 1.8 years, and the same crossing with
 τ twice as large fails about once every 1.8 years even with two
 stages. The first number is why synchronisers exist; the second is why the answer is
 always quoted with its corner.

The next chapter takes the quantity this one kept assuming — that a sample is
 either right or wrong — and replaces it with a distribution. Noise sets the floor
 under every analog measurement in a mixed-signal IP, and unlike metastability it can
 be traded directly against power and area.

특허로 가는 길 — 이 주제에서 발명이 일어나는 자리

Metastability itself is physics, and the two-flop synchroniser is older
 than anyone reading this. What is still being claimed is the arrangement
 around it: a pointer encoding that keeps a multi-bit crossing safe with one
 synchroniser instead of N (gray codes and their successors); a
 latency-versus-MTBF scheme that switches synchroniser depth by operating mode;
 a data-path crossing that avoids synchronising the data at all by synchronising
 only a qualifier and holding the data stable across the boundary. Every
 one of these is an argument about what must cross, not about the flop.
 Read this chapter asking: which of my signals actually has to cross, and what
 would let the rest stay on one side?

장: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything
절: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything — 들어가며
글:
T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything

Noise is the one specification you cannot improve with cleverness alone. Every 6 dB costs 4× the capacitance, and therefore 4× the power.

읽기 전에 알아야 하는 것
전압 · 전류 · 저항 · 온도 · 확률 · 분산 · 표준편차 · 적분 · 로그 · 주파수 · 트랜스컨덕턴스 · 게이트용량 · 출력저항 · RC지연 · 준안정

이 장에서 새로 나오는 것
열잡음 · 산탄잡음 · 플리커잡음 · 잡음스펙트럼밀도 · 잡음대역폭 · kTC잡음 · 입력환산잡음 · 플리커코너 · 잡음지수 · 정적잡음여유 · 나비곡선 · 읽기방해 · 최소동작전압 · SNR · SNDR · ENOB

Everything measured in a circuit arrives with noise on it, and the noise does
 not come from poor engineering — it comes from the thermal motion of charge and from
 the discreteness of the electron. That makes it the hardest kind of specification:
 you cannot remove it, you can only spend area and power to average it down, and the
 exchange rate is fixed by physics at 4× the cost per extra bit.

This chapter establishes the three noise sources you will actually meet, then
 derives the one number that sizes half the analog blocks in a mixed-signal IP
 (kT/C), and then does something unusual for a noise chapter: it crosses into the
 digital side, where the same word means something entirely different and where the
 consequence — the voltage below which an SRAM cannot be read — is measured here
 with ngspice rather than asserted.

장: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything
절: T4.1 The three sources, and which one you can do anything about
글:
T4.1 The three sources, and which one you can do anything about

[표 14. Noise sources in an IC, by origin]
Source | Density | Origin | Can you change it?
Thermal (Johnson) | S v = 4kTR [V²/Hz] | Thermal motion of carriers in any resistive element | Only by changing R, T, or the bandwidth you look through
Channel thermal | S i = 4kTγg m [A²/Hz] | The same mechanism inside a MOSFET channel; γ ≈ 2/3 long-channel, 1–2 short-channel | Raise g m (costs current) or filter
Flicker (1/f) | S v = K f /(C ox WL·f) | Trapping and de-trapping at the oxide interface | Yes — bigger devices, PMOS inputs, chopping, auto-zero
Shot | S i = 2qI [A²/Hz] | Discreteness of charge crossing a barrier (junctions, not channels) | Only by changing the current

유도 — Why the answer always ends up as kT/C

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | A resistor's thermal noise density is 4kTR, independent of frequency. | Nyquist's result from equilibrium thermodynamics — it contains no device parameter beyond R, which is why it is a floor and not a design choice.
2 | Put that resistor in series with a capacitor C — which is what every sampling switch is. | The switch's on-resistance (T1: triode region) and the sampling capacitor are in series; there is no third element.
3 | The RC low-pass shapes it, and the noise bandwidth of a single pole is π/2 × f −3dB = 1/(4RC). | Integrating 1/(1+(f/f 0 )²) over all frequency gives π/2·f 0 , not f 0 — a factor people drop and then wonder why measurements are 1.6× worse than predicted.
4 | v n ² = 4kTR × 1/(4RC) = kT/C. | R cancels. The noise on a sampled capacitor does not depend on the switch at all — only on C and temperature.
5 | For C = 1 pF at 3 K, v n = 64.4 µV rms. | One number worth memorising; everything else scales as 1/√C from here.

kT/C — the rule that sizes capacitors, and therefore power

A sampled node carries kT/C of noise power regardless of how it was
 sampled. To keep that below the quantisation noise of an N-bit converter
 (LSB/√12), the capacitor must satisfy C ≥ 12kT·22N/VFS².
 Every extra bit quadruples C, and because settling in a fixed time needs
 gm ∝ C, it quadruples the current too.

This single relation is why a 16-bit converter is not "a bit harder" than a
 12-bit one: it is 256× the capacitance.

어디에 쓰나 | Every switched-capacitor circuit: SAR and pipeline ADC sampling networks, sample-and-holds, switched-capacitor filters and gain stages, the reference buffer that has to drive them.
언제 쓰나 | At the very start of an analog block's design, before any transistor is sized. The capacitor comes first because it fixes the power budget.
어떻게 쓰나 | Fix V FS and N, compute C, then size the driver for settling within the sampling phase (T2's RC arithmetic with the switch's R on from T1), then check that the reference can supply the charge each cycle.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
* The measurement that separates kT/C from everything else you did wrong.
* Transient noise in ngspice: sample the same node 1000 times and take the std dev.
.tran 1n 10u
.noise v(out) VIN dec 20 1 1G $ small-signal, for the spectrum
.measure noise inoise_total_rms param='sqrt(inoise_total)'
* And the closed form to check it against -- ALWAYS have the hand calculation:
* v_n = sqrt(kT/C) = sqrt(1.38e-23*300/1e-12) = 64.4 uV for C = 1 pF
```

여기서 틀린다. kT/C applies to the sampled value. During the tracking phase the
 noise bandwidth is set by the circuit, not by the sampling — so a
 track-and-hold that is measured while tracking shows a different (usually
 larger) number than the same circuit measured after the hold. Reporting one
 when the spec means the other is a common and expensive mistake.

[표 15. Capacitor and power cost per bit (V_FS = 1 V, 300 K, noise = quantisation noise)]
Bits N | LSB | Quantisation rms | C required | Relative to 8-bit
8 | 3,906 µV | 1,128 µV | 3.26 fF | 1×
10 | 977 µV | 282 µV | 52.1 fF | 16×
12 | 244 µV | 70.5 µV | 834 fF | 256×
14 | 61 µV | 17.6 µV | 13.3 pF | 4,096×
16 | 15.3 µV | 4.4 µV | 213 pF | 65,536×

장: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything
절: T4.2 Flicker noise, and the corner that decides your architecture
글:
T4.2 Flicker noise, and the corner that decides your architecture

플리커코너 (flicker corner, f_c) — The frequency at which the 1/f density equals the thermal density. Below it the circuit is flicker-dominated, above it thermal-dominated. For a modern CMOS amplifier it lands anywhere from ~100 kHz to a few MHz for NMOS inputs, typically a decade lower for PMOS.

Where the signal sits relative to the corner

Flicker noise density rises as 1/f, so its integrated power over a
 band from f1 to f2 is proportional to ln(f2/f1)
 — it depends on the ratio, not the width. A DC-coupled measurement has
 f1 → 0 and the integral diverges logarithmically: the longer you
 average, the worse it gets, which is the opposite of thermal noise.

That single fact drives an architectural decision. If the signal is near DC
 (a temperature sensor, a bandgap reference, a DC offset), averaging does not
 help and you must move the signal — chop it up to a frequency above the
 corner, amplify there, and bring it back down. If the signal is already above
 the corner (an RF or high-speed link front end), flicker is irrelevant and you
 spend nothing on it.

어디에 쓰나 | Sensor front ends, reference and bias circuits, comparator offset, any DC-accurate measurement. Also the phase noise of an oscillator, where device flicker is up-converted into close-in phase noise.
언제 쓰나 | Whenever the band of interest includes frequencies below ~1 MHz. Ask the question explicitly at architecture time; retrofitting chopping into a finished amplifier is a redesign.
어떻게 쓰나 | Reduce it by area (S ∝ 1/WL — 4× the area for 6 dB), by choosing PMOS inputs, or by modulation: chopping (square-wave modulate in and out; leaves residual ripple at the chop frequency) or correlated double sampling (sample the offset, subtract it; costs noise folding and bandwidth).

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
* Flicker in the model card is one parameter -- and simulators differ.
.model NM NMOS (LEVEL=54 ... KF=1e-25 AF=1.0 EF=1.0)
* KF alone means nothing: the density is KF/(Cox*W*L*f^EF), so a KF taken from
* another PDK, or from a model with a different EF convention, is a WRONG number
* that still simulates. Always sanity-check the corner against measured silicon:
.noise v(out) VIN dec 10 1 100MEG
* then read the point where the 1/f asymptote crosses the flat part.
```

여기서 틀린다. Chopping does not reduce noise; it moves the signal away from the
 noise. The thermal floor is unchanged and the chopper adds its own
 switching artefacts at the chop frequency and its harmonics. A design that
 reports a beautiful low-frequency noise figure and a spur at fchop
 has not improved anything if the spur lands in band.

장: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything
절: T4.3 The other noise: static noise margin, measured
글:
T4.3 The other noise: static noise margin, measured

On the digital side the word 'noise' means something different and the
 quantity is not a spectral density but a voltage: how much DC disturbance a
 storage node can absorb before it flips. The structure is the same cross-coupled pair
 that produced metastability in T3, viewed statically instead of dynamically.

정적잡음여유 (SNM, static noise margin) — The largest DC voltage that can be inserted in series with both storage nodes of a cross-coupled pair without destroying its bistability. Geometrically it is the side of the largest square that fits inside the butterfly curve formed by the two inverter transfer curves.

실제로 난 일
The extractor used below was wrong twice before it was right,
 and both times the numbers looked plausible. The first version measured a horizontal
 gap instead of an inscribed square and reported hold SNM ≈ 0.5·VDD — too
 high. The second version had the access transistor wired with its gate on the bitline
 instead of the word line; it produced read SNM that fell as the cell ratio
 rose, which is backwards. The trend caught the bug, not the value. That is the
 rule this repository runs on: before believing a measurement, check the direction it
 moves when you change something you understand.

The extractor was then self-checked against two limits: an
 inverter with very high gain must give SNM → VDD/2 (it gives 0.4825) and
 an 'inverter' with gain 1 must give 0 (it gives 0.0). Only after both did the cell
 numbers below get written down.

[표 16. Measured SNM of a 6T cell (ngspice, LEVEL=1 model, V_DD = 1.0 V, V_th = 0.35 V) — β is the cell ratio W_pulldown / W_access]
β | Hold SNM | Read SNM | Read / Hold
1 | 0.421 V | 0.194 V | 0.46
1.5 | 0.417 V | 0.207 V | 0.5
2 | 0.414 V | 0.226 V | 0.55
2.5 | 0.411 V | 0.241 V | 0.59
3 | 0.409 V | 0.253 V | 0.62

[그림] 그림 9. Reading costs more than half the cell's margin, and the only structural way to buy it back is a stronger pull-down relative to the access device — which is why the 6T cell is not made of minimum devices.

유도 — Why reading a cell is what almost destroys it

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | To read, the word line turns on both access transistors while both bit lines are precharged high. | That is the only way to sense the cell without a separate read port.
2 | The access transistor on the '0' side now pulls that node up , through a divider formed with the cell's own pull-down NMOS. | Two NMOS devices in series between V DD and ground, with the storage node in the middle — the node cannot stay at 0 V.
3 | The '0' node rises to roughly V DD ·(1/(1+β)) in the resistive limit, so a β of 2 already puts it a third of the way up. | Both devices are in triode at that point; the ratio of their strengths is the divider ratio. This is the only reason the cell ratio exists as a design parameter.
4 | That rise eats directly into the margin: measured read SNM at β = 2 is 0.226 V against a hold SNM of 0.414 V — 45.3 % of the margin is gone the moment the word line rises. | Measured, not asserted — the deck and the extractor are in this chapter's source.
5 | Raising β raises read SNM and slightly lowers hold SNM . | Measured: hold falls from 0.421 V to 0.409 V across the same sweep, because a stronger pull-down skews each inverter's trip point away from V DD /2. There is no free direction , which is what makes it a design point rather than a rule.

V_min — the voltage at which the memory, not the logic, stops the chip

Read SNM does not degrade gracefully with supply. Measured on the same
 cell at β = 2, it holds near 0.22 V from 1.0 V down to 0.7 V
 and then collapses: 0.145 V at 0.6 V and
 0.087 V at 0.5 V. The knee sits where VDD approaches
 2Vth (0.7 V here) — below that the devices are in weak
 inversion, the divider ratio depends on exponential currents, and mismatch
 (T12) turns a marginal cell into a failing one.

This is why the SRAM sets the chip's minimum operating voltage, and
 why DVFS schemes either stop above the array's Vmin or give the array
 its own supply.

어디에 쓰나 | Any SoC with on-chip SRAM and more than one voltage point: the whole DVFS range, retention voltage in sleep modes, and the low-voltage corner in signoff.
언제 쓰나 | As soon as a power mode is proposed. The question 'can we drop to 0.6 V' is an SRAM question before it is a logic question.
어떻게 쓰나 | Either raise V min with assist circuits (word-line underdrive for read, negative bit line for write), split the array's supply, or use an 8T cell where the read path does not touch the storage node.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
* The sweep that produces the number above -- run it at every corner,
* not just typical, because Vmin is a MISMATCH-limited quantity (see T12).
.param beta=2.0
.dc VIN 0 VDD 0.004 VDD 1.0 0.5 -0.1 $ nested sweep: input, then supply
.print dc v(vr)
* Extraction is NOT a .measure one-liner: you need the butterfly and the largest
* inscribed square. Script it, and SELF-CHECK the extractor on two limits
* (very high gain -> VDD/2, gain 1 -> 0) before trusting any cell number.
```

여기서 틀린다. SNM measured at the typical corner is nearly useless for Vmin.
 The array fails at its worst cell out of millions, so the quantity
 that matters is the tail: Vmin is set by roughly the −5σ to −6σ
 cell, which means the analysis is a Monte Carlo with importance sampling,
 not a nominal DC sweep. The sweep above tells you the shape; it does not
 tell you the yield.

장: T4. Noise — and Why It Sets the Size of Everything
절: T4.4 From volts to a datasheet number: SNR, SNDR, ENOB
글:
T4.4 From volts to a datasheet number: SNR, SNDR, ENOB

[표 17. The three numbers, and what each one hides]
Quantity | Definition | Hides
SNR | Signal power / noise power, distortion excluded | Distortion. A converter with terrible linearity can have excellent SNR
SNDR (SINAD) | Signal / (noise + all distortion) | Which of the two dominates — always report the spectrum too
ENOB | (SNDR dB − 1.76) / 6.02 | That it is derived , not measured. ENOB is SNDR wearing different units; an ENOB quoted without its input frequency and amplitude is not a measurement
SFDR | Signal / largest single spur | Broadband noise entirely — a clean-looking SFDR with a poor noise floor is common

예제 5. How many bits does 64 µV of noise allow?

주어진 것. A 1 V full-scale converter with C = 1 pF on its sampling network, so the
 sampled noise is 64.4 µV rms, and assume everything else
 is perfect.

푸는 법. A full-scale sine has rms amplitude VFS/(2√2). SNR =
 20·log10(signal rms / noise rms), then ENOB = (SNR − 1.76)/6.02.

답. SNR = 74.8 dB,
 giving ENOB = 12.1
 bits. A 1 pF sampling capacitor is a ~12-bit part, no matter how good the
 rest of the design is.

여기서 틀린다. Forgetting that the sampling network is usually sampled twice (input
 and reference), and that a differential pair of capacitors doubles the noise
 power while doubling the signal amplitude — the two partly cancel, and the
 factor you get depends on the topology. Write the specific network down; do not
 reuse a remembered factor.

절: T4.5 What to do with this on Monday
글:
T4.5 What to do with this on Monday

[표 18. 이 장의 개념이 실제로 쓰이는 자리]
개념 | 쓰이는 블록 | 무엇을 정하나
kTC잡음 | Any switched-capacitor block, before sizing transistors | The sampling capacitor, and therefore the current budget
열잡음 · 잡음대역폭 | Amplifier and reference design | How much g m the input stage needs

Two measured results to carry out of this chapter. A 1 pF sampling capacitor

 the capacitor decides the resolution before any transistor is drawn. And reading a
 6T SRAM cell costs
 45.3 % of its static margin at a
 cell ratio of 2, which is why that cell ratio exists and why the array, not the
 logic, sets the lowest voltage the chip can run at.

The next chapter takes the sampling operation that this one treated as
 instantaneous and gives it a finite aperture, a jitter, and a spectrum — which is

특허로 가는 길 — 이 주제에서 발명이 일어나는 자리

Noise is thermodynamics; nobody patents kT. What gets claimed is
 every arrangement that buys back the 4× — correlated double sampling, chopping,
 auto-zeroing, noise shaping, and the family of techniques that let a circuit
 spend its noise budget only where the signal is. On the digital side the
 same shape appears as assist circuits for SRAM: negative bitline, word-line
 underdrive, read-modify-write assist — all of them arrangements that let a cell
 keep its margin at a voltage where the plain cell has none. Read this chapter
 asking: where am I paying the 4× rule, and what would let me not pay it?

장: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number
절: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number — 들어가며
글:
T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number

Two clocks decide everything: when you sample, and how precisely you know when. The second one is what limits every high-speed converter shipping today.

읽기 전에 알아야 하는 것
전압 · 주파수 · 위상 · 적분 · 미분 · 확률 · 표준편차 · 로그 · RC지연 · 슬루 · kTC잡음 · 열잡음 · SNR · SNDR · ENOB · 잡음대역폭

이 장에서 새로 나오는 것
표본화정리 · 엘리어싱 · 나이키스트 · 대역통과표본화 · 구경시간 · 구경지터 · 지터한계SNR · 추적유지 · 트래킹대역폭 · 차지인젝션 · 클럭피드스루 · 부트스트랩스위치 · 오버샘플링비 · 잡음성형 · 데시메이션

Sampling is usually taught as an idealisation — multiply by an impulse train,
 observe the spectrum repeat, avoid overlap. That story is correct and it is not the
 one that limits hardware. A real sampler closes a switch for a finite time, through
 a finite resistance, at an instant known only to within some picoseconds, onto a
 capacitor whose size was already fixed by kT/C in T4. Each of those four words —
 finite, finite, instant, capacitor — costs resolution, and the one that dominates
 above a few hundred megahertz is the third.

장: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number
절: T5.1 Aliasing is not a theorem you obey, it is a filter you buy
글:
T5.1 Aliasing is not a theorem you obey, it is a filter you buy

유도 — From the impulse train to the folded spectrum

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | Sampling at f s multiplies the signal by a train of impulses spaced T s = 1/f s . | The idealisation. Everything about aliasing follows from this one step; the non-idealities come later and do not change it.
2 | Multiplication in time is convolution in frequency, and the impulse train's spectrum is itself an impulse train spaced f s . | So the input spectrum is copied to every multiple of f s .
3 | Copies overlap unless the input is confined to a band narrower than f s /2. | Nyquist. Note what it does not say: it says nothing about where the band sits, only how wide it is.
4 | Everything above f s /2 folds down and is indistinguishable from a real signal afterwards. | No digital processing can undo it — the information that told the two apart was destroyed at the sampler. This is why an anti-alias filter is an analog component and cannot be moved into software.
5 | Noise folds too , and by the same rule. | A front end with 5 GHz of bandwidth sampled at 200 MHz folds 50 bands of thermal noise onto the signal — a 17 dB penalty. Bandwidth you do not need is not free ; it is noise you pay for.

Bandpass sampling — using the folding on purpose

Nyquist constrains the width of the band, not its position. A signal
 occupying 100 MHz centred at 2.4 GHz can be sampled at 250 MS/s, provided the
 band falls entirely inside one Nyquist zone and the sampler's input bandwidth
 reaches 2.4 GHz. The alias is the wanted signal, translated down for
 free.

The cost is precise: the sampling aperture must be good enough for
 2.4 GHz even though the sample rate is 250 MHz — jitter is referred to the input
 frequency, not the clock rate. That trade (no mixer, but a far harder clock) is
 the whole engineering decision.

어디에 쓰나 | RF receivers that digitise at IF, software-defined radio front ends, and any instrument that must capture a narrow band sitting at a high frequency.
언제 쓰나 | When the band is narrow relative to its centre frequency and you would otherwise pay for a downconversion mixer and its LO.
어떻게 쓰나 | Pick f s so the band lands strictly inside a single zone (k·f s /2 to (k+1)·f s /2), add a bandpass anti-alias filter — a low-pass is useless here — and budget the jitter against the RF carrier.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
// Zone check, written as an assertion rather than a comment.
// A band that straddles a zone boundary is a silent failure: it still samples,
// and the output is two overlapped copies.
localparam real FS = 250e6, FC = 2.4e9, BW = 100e6;
initial begin
 int k = $floor(2.0*(FC - BW/2)/FS);
 assert ($floor(2.0*(FC + BW/2)/FS) == k)
 else $fatal(1, "band straddles a Nyquist zone boundary -- pick another FS");
end
```

여기서 틀린다. The anti-alias filter for bandpass sampling must reject every other
 zone, not just frequencies above fs/2. Engineers who reuse a
 low-pass filter here get a receiver that works in the lab (where the only
 signal present is the wanted one) and fails in the field.

장: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number
절: T5.2 Aperture jitter — the wall
글:
T5.2 Aperture jitter — the wall

구경지터 (aperture jitter) — The rms uncertainty in the instant at which the sampler actually captures the signal. It comes from the clock path (phase noise, supply-induced delay modulation, thermal noise in the last buffer) and from the sampler itself, and it is referred to the input frequency, not the sample rate.

유도 — Why jitter costs more as the signal gets faster

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | A sine v(t) = A·sin(2πf in t) has slope dv/dt = 2πf in A·cos(…). | The slope is what converts a time error into a voltage error — this is the whole mechanism.
2 | A timing error Δt therefore produces a voltage error Δv = (dv/dt)·Δt, worst at the zero crossing where the slope is greatest. | The largest error happens where the signal is changing fastest, not where it is largest.
3 | With rms jitter σ t and a full-scale sine, the rms error is 2πf in ·(A/√2)·σ t , and the signal rms is A/√2. | The amplitude cancels — jitter-limited SNR does not depend on signal amplitude , which is why you cannot back away from it by scaling down.
4 | SNR = −20·log 10 (2πf in σ t ). | One equation, two variables, no device parameters. It is a property of the clock and the input frequency alone.
5 | At f in = 1 GHz, 100 fs of jitter gives 64 dB — 10.3 bits. | 100 fs is already a hard clock. This is why 12-bit gigahertz converters are difficult in a way that has nothing to do with the comparator.

[표 19. Jitter-limited SNR and ENOB (uncorrelated aperture jitter only)]
f_in | 1 ps | 300 fs | 100 fs | 30 fs
0.1 GHz | 64.0 dB / 10.3 b | 74.5 dB / 12.1 b | 84.0 dB / 13.7 b | 94.5 dB / 15.4 b
1 GHz | 44.0 dB / 7.0 b | 54.5 dB / 8.8 b | 64.0 dB / 10.3 b | 74.5 dB / 12.1 b
5 GHz | 30.1 dB / 4.7 b | 40.5 dB / 6.4 b | 50.1 dB / 8.0 b | 60.5 dB / 9.8 b

예제 6. What clock does a 12-bit, 1 GHz-input converter need?

주어진 것. The design target is 12 effective bits at a 1 GHz input. Assume jitter is the
 only error source — an optimistic assumption that makes the answer a lower
 bound on how good the clock must be.

푸는 법. Invert the SNR expression: σt = 1/(2π·fin·2N).

답. σt = 38.9 fs rms. For 14 bits it is
 9.71 fs.

[표 20. Required rms aperture jitter at f_in = 1 GHz]
Bits | σ_t required
8 | 622 fs
10 | 155 fs
12 | 38.9 fs
14 | 9.71 fs
16 | 2.43 fs

여기서 틀린다. Comparing that number against the jitter quoted for a clock source.
 The specification that matters is the jitter at the sampling switch,
 after the whole distribution path — buffers, level shifters, the divider, and
 whatever supply noise the digital side injected into them. A 20 fs source
 behind a noisy buffer chain is a 200 fs sampler, and the datasheet of the source
 will not tell you that.

Jitter and kT/C add in power, not in amplitude, and they scale
 in opposite directions with frequency: kT/C is flat while jitter worsens by 6 dB per
 octave of input frequency. There is therefore always a crossover frequency, and
 knowing which side of it you are on tells you which knob does anything. Below it,
 spend area on capacitance. Above it, spend power on the clock — a bigger sampling
 capacitor buys nothing in a jitter-limited design, and it is the most common way
 to waste a redesign.

장: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number
절: T5.3 The switch itself: charge injection, feedthrough, and bootstrapping
글:
T5.3 The switch itself: charge injection, feedthrough, and bootstrapping

VDD
[그림] 그림 10. The sampling switch. Its on-resistance sets the tracking bandwidth; its channel charge lands on the sampling capacitor when it turns off.

[표 21. Three errors the switch adds, and what each depends on]
Error | Mechanism | Scales with | Signal-dependent?
Charge injection | The channel's inversion charge has to go somewhere when the device turns off; roughly half lands on C s | W·L·C ox ·(V GS −V th ) / C s | Yes — V GS depends on the sampled level, so it becomes distortion, not offset
Clock feedthrough | C gd couples the falling clock edge onto the capacitor | C ov /(C ov +C s ) · V clk | No (to first order) — mostly a fixed offset
R on modulation | The switch's on-resistance depends on V GS = V clk − v in | 1/(μC ox (W/L)(V GS −V th )) | Yes — a signal-dependent time constant is signal-dependent settling, which is distortion

The bootstrapped switch

Hold the switch's gate at vin + VDD instead of at
 VDD, using a capacitor pre-charged to VDD and flipped onto
 the gate during the tracking phase. Then VGS is constant regardless
 of the signal, so Ron is constant and the charge injected at turn-off
 is constant — signal-dependent errors become offsets, and offsets are
 harmless in a differential design.

It also solves a reliability problem that is easy to miss: without
 bootstrapping, a switch passing a signal near ground sees VGS =
 VDD, which in an advanced node may exceed the oxide's rating over
 the device's lifetime (T14).

어디에 쓰나 | The input sampling network of essentially every SAR and pipeline ADC above 10 bits, and in high-linearity switched-capacitor filters.
언제 쓰나 | When THD or SFDR matters more than area. A plain NMOS switch is fine for 8 bits and hopeless at 12.
어떻게 쓰나 | Size the bootstrap capacitor ≫ the gate capacitance it must drive, check the reliability of every node across the clock phases, and verify distortion with a two-tone transient, not a single tone — intermodulation exposes the residual signal dependence a single tone hides.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
* The check that matters, and the one people skip.
* A single tone can look clean while IM3 is terrible.
Vin1 in1 0 SIN(0 0.45 100.1MEG)
Vin2 in2 0 SIN(0 0.45 103.3MEG)
.tran 10p 20u
.four 100.1MEG v(sampled) $ harmonic distortion
* and post-process the FFT for IM3 at 2*f1-f2 = 96.9 MHz -- the number the
* customer will measure and the one that exposes Ron modulation.
```

여기서 틀린다. Bootstrapping makes the gate voltage exceed the supply, so every node in
 the bootstrap network must be checked against the oxide limit at the
 fast, high-voltage, low-temperature corner — the opposite corner from
 the one that limits performance. A bootstrap circuit verified only at
 typical is a reliability report waiting to happen.

장: T5. Sampling — Where a Continuous Signal Becomes a Number
절: T5.4 Oversampling: buying bits with time
글:
T5.4 Oversampling: buying bits with time

유도 — Why oversampling helps, and how much

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | Quantisation noise power is LSB²/12 regardless of the sample rate . | The quantiser does not know how fast it is being clocked; the error per sample has the same distribution.
2 | That fixed power is spread over the Nyquist band, 0 to f s /2. | So the noise density is LSB²/12 divided by f s /2 — sampling faster dilutes it.
3 | Filtering down to the signal band B keeps only the fraction 2B/f s of it. | Define the oversampling ratio OSR = f s /(2B).
4 | SNR improves by 10·log 10 (OSR): 3 dB, or half a bit, per doubling . | This is plain oversampling, with no feedback. Going from 8 to 12 bits this way needs OSR = 256 — expensive but occasionally the right answer for a slow sensor.
5 | A ΔΣ modulator shapes the noise instead of merely spreading it, giving (6L+3) dB per doubling for an L-th-order loop. | The loop pushes quantisation noise out of the band. A 2nd-order modulator gains 15 dB per octave of OSR — this is why ΔΣ dominates audio and precision sensing, and why it is useless at gigahertz signal bandwidths.

[표 22. What oversampling buys, per doubling of OSR]
Architecture | SNR gain per 2× OSR | Bits per 2× OSR | Where it wins
Plain oversampling + decimation | 3 dB | 0.5 | Cheap resolution on slow signals; anti-alias filter relief
ΔΣ, 1st order | 9 dB | 1.5 | Simple, but idle tones
ΔΣ, 2nd order | 15 dB | 2.5 | Audio, precision sensors
ΔΣ, 3rd+ order / MASH | 21 dB+ | 3.5+ | Where stability engineering is worth it

Oversampling relieves the anti-alias filter as much as it buys
 resolution, and that is often the real reason to do it. Sampling a 20 kHz audio band
 at 44.1 kHz demands a filter that is flat at 20 kHz and dead at 22.05 kHz — a brutal
 analog problem. Sampling at 2.8 MHz moves the requirement to 'dead at 1.4 MHz',
 which is a single RC. The filter that disappears is usually worth more than the
 half-bit.

글:

[표 23. 이 장의 개념이 실제로 쓰이는 자리]
개념 | 쓰이는 블록 | 무엇을 정하나
엘리어싱 · 나이키스트 | Choosing f_s and the anti-alias filter | The filter order — and whether it is analog or can be shared with oversampling

The number to carry: at a 1 GHz input, 12 effective bits requires
 38.9 fs rms of aperture jitter, measured at the
 switch and not at the clock source. Every architecture decision in a high-speed
 converter — interleaving, bandpass sampling, where the clock buffer sits — is
 downstream of that one line.

The next chapter turns the sampled voltage into a code, and finds that the
 architectures differ less in accuracy than in where they spend the same
 fundamental limits.

특허로 가는 길 — 이 주제에서 발명이 일어나는 자리

The sampling instant is the most contested square millimetre in a
 high-speed converter, and the patents show it: bootstrapped switches that hold
 VGS constant so the on-resistance does not depend on the signal;
 clock paths that deliberately do not share a buffer with anything else;
 sampling schemes that cancel charge injection by symmetry rather than by
 trimming; and, one level up, time-interleaved architectures whose entire
 difficulty is that each slice samples at a slightly wrong instant. Every one
 of these is an argument about the aperture, not about the amplifier.

장: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits
절: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits — 들어가며
글:
T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits

No architecture beats kT/C, jitter or mismatch. They differ in which one they pay first, and that is the entire basis on which you choose.

읽기 전에 알아야 하는 것
전압 · 전류 · 전하 · 확률 · 표준편차 · 로그 · SNR · SNDR · ENOB · kTC잡음 · 구경지터 · 표본화정리 · 오버샘플링비 · 잡음성형 · 차지인젝션 · 정적잡음여유

이 장에서 새로 나오는 것
플래시ADC · 축차비교ADC · 파이프라인ADC · 시간인터리브 · 용량DAC · 전류구동DAC · 세그먼테이션 · INL · DNL · 미싱코드 · 단조성 · 중복성 · 디지털보정 · 글리치에너지

Converter architecture looks like a catalogue and is really a single
 question: given a resolution and a sample rate, which fundamental limit do you hit
 first, and which architecture lets you pay that one in the currency you have? Every
 architecture faces the same kT/C, the same jitter, the same mismatch. What differs
 is how many times per conversion each limit is paid.

장: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits
절: T6.1 The map, and what sets each boundary
글:
T6.1 The map, and what sets each boundary

[표 24. The four architectures, and the limit that stops each]
Architecture | Comparisons per sample | Practical range | What stops it
Flash | 2 N − 1 in parallel | 4–8 b, up to tens of GS/s | Area and input capacitance double per bit; 2 N comparator offsets must each be worse, because three new
 error terms appear that do not exist in a single converter. Timing skew between
 slices is the hardest: it is a jitter problem (T5) that is deterministic, so
 it produces spurs rather than a noise floor, and a spur at a predictable frequency
 is exactly what a customer's spectrum plot will show.

장: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits
절: T6.2 The SAR's capacitor array: where matching beats noise
글:
T6.2 The SAR's capacitor array: where matching beats noise

A SAR converter is a binary search implemented with a capacitive DAC. Its
 accuracy therefore rests on capacitor ratios, and the design question is simply how
 big the unit capacitor must be. Two independent requirements set it, and which one
 wins is not obvious until you compute both.

유도 — Two requirements on the same capacitor, and where they cross

 | 이렇게 된다 | 왜냐하면
1 | Requirement 1 — noise : the array is the sampling capacitor, so kT/C total must stay below the quantisation noise (T4). | For 1 V full scale this gives C ≥ 12kT·2 2N /V FS ²: 0.83 pF at 12 bits.
2 | Requirement 2 — matching : DNL at the mid-scale transition is dominated by the mismatch of the largest capacitor against the sum of the rest. | 3σ DNL u /C u area .
3 | A capacitor that matches to that level is about 1 fF in a modern MOM-capacitor process, which makes the 12-bit array 4.1 pF — 4.91× larger than the noise requirement. | At 12 bits the array is set by matching, not by noise. Sizing it from kT/C alone gives a converter with an excellent noise floor and visible DNL steps.
4 | At 14 bits the two requirements are 16.4 pF and 13.3 pF — they have converged. | Above ~14 bits noise takes over and the unit capacitor can be whatever matches; below it, matching rules. Knowing which side you are on tells you which knob does anything.

[표 25. Which limit sizes the SAR array (V_FS = 1 V, unit cap 1 fF)]
Bits | Matching needs σ_u/C_u overlap — each step can correct an earlier error of up
 to the overlap.

The cost is one or two extra cycles; the benefit is that early cycles no
 longer need to settle to the full N-bit accuracy, only to within the overlap.
 Since settling time is logarithmic in accuracy (T2), relaxing the early
 cycles is most of the conversion time.

어디에 쓰나 | Every modern high-speed SAR, and the inter-stage stages of pipelines (where it is called 1.5-bit-per-stage).
언제 쓰나 | Whenever the conversion must be fast. It is nearly free in area and it is the difference between a 10 MS/s and a 100 MS/s SAR at the same resolution.
어떻게 쓰나 | Choose a sub-binary radix (e.g. 1.86 instead of 2), size the capacitors accordingly, and reconstruct the output digitally with the correction weights. The weights can also be calibrated , which turns capacitor mismatch into a measured constant rather than an error.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
// Non-binary SAR reconstruction. The weights are NOT powers of two,
// and they are per-chip once calibration has run.
localparam int W [0:N] = '{2048, 1088, 576, 320, 176, 96, 56, 32, 18, 10, 6, 4, 2, 1};
always_comb begin
 code = 0;
 for (int i = 0; i 여기서 틀린다. Redundancy protects against incomplete settling and comparator
 noise, not against a DAC that is monotonically wrong. If a capacitor is
 mis-sized beyond the overlap, redundancy hides the symptom in simple tests
 and leaves a code-dependent error that only a full INL sweep reveals.

장: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits
절: T6.3 Static linearity: INL, DNL, and the two ways a converter lies
글:
T6.3 Static linearity: INL, DNL, and the two ways a converter lies

DNL (차등 비선형성) — The deviation of each code's width from 1 LSB. DNL = −1 LSB means the code has zero width — a missing code, and the converter is no longer monotonic there.

INL (적분 비선형성) — The cumulative deviation of each transition point from the ideal straight line — the running sum of DNL. It is what distortion measurements see; DNL is what a control loop feels.

[표 26. Which one to care about, and when]
Application | The one that matters | Why
Audio / RF spectrum | INL | Curvature is distortion; the customer's FFT shows harmonics
Closed-loop control (e.g. a DAC in a servo) | DNL and monotonicity | A non-monotonic code inverts the loop's sign locally and can oscillate
Sensor threshold detection | DNL | A missing code is a value the system can never report
Digital calibration of another block | INL | The correction is only as good as the reference curve

실제로 난 일
A converter can pass an SNDR test and be badly non-monotonic. A
 sine-wave histogram test averages over all codes; a single missing code moves SNDR
 by a fraction of a dB and is invisible. Static linearity needs its own test —
 a slow ramp or a code-density sweep — and an IP deliverable that reports only SNDR
 has not characterised the part.

장: T6. Data Converters — Where Each Architecture Spends the Same Limits
절: T6.4 The DAC side: segmentation and glitch energy
글:
T6.4 The DAC side: segmentation and glitch energy

세그먼테이션 (segmentation) — thermometer where it matters, binary where it does not

A fully binary DAC has the worst possible glitch at mid-scale: every
 switch changes at once, and their timing skew produces a transient whose area
 (glitch energy, in V·s) does not average out — it appears as distortion
 at the update rate. A fully thermometer-coded DAC has no such transition but
 needs 2N−1 elements and the decoder to drive them.

Real DACs segment: the top M bits thermometer, the rest binary. M is chosen
 so that the largest simultaneous switching event is small enough, and the
 practical answer is usually 4–6 — the decoder cost grows as 2M while
 the glitch improvement saturates.

어디에 쓰나 | Current-steering DACs for transmitters and waveform generators; the reference DACs inside pipeline ADCs; any DAC whose output is observed in the frequency domain.
언제 쓰나 | Whenever SFDR is specified. A binary DAC's mid-scale glitch usually sets SFDR before any static error does.
어떻게 쓰나 | Segment the MSBs, match the unit current sources by layout (common centroid, dummies), and randomise or rotate the selection of unit elements (DEM) so residual mismatch becomes noise instead of a spur.

실제 코드는 이렇게 생겼다

```
// Segmented decode: 6 thermometer MSBs + 8 binary LSBs.
// The point of the thermometer part is that consecutive codes change ONE element.
logic [62:0] therm;
always_comb begin
 therm = '0;
 for (int i = 0; i i);
end
// Dynamic element matching: rotate the starting index so that element mismatch
// is spread across codes and appears as a raised noise floor, not as a spur.
always_ff @(posedge clk) rot > rot; // barrel rotate
```

여기서 틀린다. DEM converts a spur into noise — it does not remove the error. If the
 spectrum requirement is a noise floor, that is a win; if it is total noise
 power, it is neutral. Reporting 'SFDR improved by 15 dB' after enabling DEM
 without also reporting the noise floor is the kind of half-truth a customer
 finds in their own lab.

절: T6.5 What to do with this on Monday
글:
T6.5 What to do with this on Monday

[표 27. 이 장의 개념이 실제로 쓰이는 자리]
개념 | 쓰이는 블록 | 무엇을 정하나
플래시 · 축차비교 · 파이프라인 · 시간인터리브 | Architecture selection, first week | Which limit you will be paying
